text: Flexor and Extensor Muscles [Lat. flectere , to bend, and extendere , to stretch out]: Ger. Beugmuskel , Streckmuskel ; Fr. muscle fléchisseur , muscle extenseur ; Ital. muscolo flessore ed estensore . Muscles that either bend (flexor) or straighten out (extensor) a joint. A pair of muscles, one flexor and the other extensor, are called antagonistic muscles. Cf. ANTAGONISM. A common German expression is 'Beuger und Strecker.' For a list of flexor and extensor muscles see Quain's Anatomy . ( C.F.H. )
